{{nihongo|'''Inbe- Shrine'''|忌部神社}} is a [[shinto shrine]] in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]]. It is located in [[Awa Province (Tokushima)]].

=== Enshrined deity ===
* {{ill|Otori-sama|Q10939697|qid=Q10939697|lt=Ame-no-Hiwashi-no-Mikoto}} (あめのひわしのみこと)
An ancestral deity of the Awa {{ill|Inbe clan|fa|خاندان اینبه|ja|忌部氏|pl|Inbe (ród)|simple|Inbe clan|th|ตระกูลอิมเบะ|zh|忌部氏|qid=Q8189229}}, and according to ''{{ill|Kogo Shūi|Q531555|qid=Q531555}}'', at the time of Amaterasu’s hiding in the rock cave, he followed {{ill|Futodama|it|Futodama|ja|フトダマ|ru|Футодама|simple|Futodama|zh|布刀玉命|qid=Q11059539|lt=Ame-no-Futodama-no-Mikoto}}, planted {{ill|Paper mulberry|an|Broussonetia papyrifera|ar|توت الورق|arz|بروسونته ورقيه|az|Kağız kağızağacı|azb|کاغیزی آغاج|be|Broussonetia papyrifera|ca|Morera de paper|ceb|Broussonetia papyrifera|cs|Papírovník čínský|de|Papiermaulbeerbaum|el|Βρουσονέτια η παπυροφόρος|es|Broussonetia papyrifera|eu|Paper-masustondo|fa|توت کاغذی|fi|Paperimulperio|fr|Broussonetia papyrifera|he|תות נייר|hu|Kínai papíreperfa|hy|Բրուսոնեթիա թղթյա|id|Daluang|it|Broussonetia papyrifera|ja|カジノキ|ko|꾸지나무|la|Broussonetia papyrifera|lfn|Morero turces|mad|Dhâlubâng|mi|Aute|mk|Broussonetia papyrifera|ml|പേപ്പർ മൾബെറി|ms|Jeluang|my|သာလဲပင်|nl|Papiermoerbei|no|Papirmorbærtre|pl|Brusonecja chińska|pt|Amoreira-do-papel|pwn|quljicaca|ru|Бруссонетия бумажная|simple|Paper mulberry|sr|Дудовац|su|Daluang|sv|Pappersmullbärsträd|th|ปอสา|tl|Papel moras|to|Hiapo|tr|Broussonetia papyrifera|uk|Broussonetia papyrifera|vi|Dướng|war|Broussonetia papyrifera|zh|構樹|zh_min_nan|Lo̍k-á-chhiū|zh_yue|構樹|qid=Q389185|lt=kaji trees}}, and made white cloth offerings woven from {{ill|Broussonetia kazinoki × B. papyrifera|ar|بروسونتة كازينوكية|arz|بروسونته كازينوكيه|az|Kazinok kağızağacı|ceb|Broussonetia kazinoki|fr|Broussonetia kazinoki|ja|コウゾ|ko|닥나무|ru|Бруссонетия Казинока|sv|Broussonetia kazinoki|vi|Broussonetia kazinoki|war|Broussonetia kazinoki|zh|楮构|qid=Q4097283}} fibers (also called {{ill|yū cloth|ja|木綿 (ゆう)|qid=Q11519320}}).

=== History ===
The “Inbe Shrine of Oe District, Awa Province” listed in the {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|Q11064932|qid=Q11064932}} had also been a myōjin taisha, but after the medieval period its location became unknown due to warfare and other causes. Since multiple shrines claimed to be the shikinaisha Inbe Shrine in early modern times, in {{ill|1871|Q7746|qid=Q7746}} (Meiji 4) it was provisionally ranked kokuhei chūsha with “location unknown,” and in the next year the village shrine {{ill|Inbe Shrine (Yoshinogawa)|Q11490723|qid=Q11490723|lt=Inbe Shrine}} in Yamazaki village, Oe District (now Yamakawa-chō, {{ill|Yoshinogawa, Tokushima|Q592500|qid=Q592500}}), was designated as the shikinaisha Inbe Shrine.

In response, Goshō Shrine at Nishibatayama in {{ill|Mima District, Tokushima|ceb|Mima Gun|es|Distrito de Mima|fr|District de Mima|id|Distrik Mima, Tokushima|it|Distretto di Mima|ja|美馬郡|ko|미마군|pl|Powiat Mima|uk|Повіт Міма|zh|美馬郡|qid=Q1156496}} (now Sadamitsu, {{ill|Tsurugi, Tokushima|arz|تسوروجى|ceb|Tsurugi Chō|es|Tsurugi (Tokushima)|fa|تسوروگی، توکوشیما|fr|Tsurugi (Tokushima)|id|Tsurugi, Tokushima|it|Tsurugi (Tokushima)|ja|つるぎ町|ko|쓰루기정|ms|Tsurugi, Tokushima|my|ဆွတ်ရုဂိမြို့|pl|Tsurugi (Tokushima)|ru|Цуруги (посёлок)|sv|Tsurugi, Tokushima|tl|Tsurugi, Tokushima|tr|Tsurugi|uk|Цуруґі (Токусіма)|uz|Tsurugi (Tokushima)|zh|劍町|qid=Q1206005}}; now this shrine’s external {{ill|Sessha|Q135009904|qid=Q135009904}} {{ill|Gosho Shrine|Q119929720|qid=Q119929720|lt=Goshō Shrine}}) asserted that claim. Although in {{ill|1874|ab|1874|af|1874|als|1874|am|1874 እ.ኤ.አ.|an|1874|ar|1874|ary|1874|arz|1874|ast|1874|avk|1874|az|1874|azb|۱۸۷۴ (میلادی)|ba|1874 йыл|ban|1874|bar|1874|bat_smg|1874|bcl|1874|be|1874|be_x_old|1874|bg|1874|bn|১৮৭৪|bpy|মারি ১৮৭৪|br|1874|bs|1874.|ca|1874|cdo|1874 nièng|ce|1874 шо|ceb|1874|ckb|١٨٧٤|crh|1874|cs|1874|csb|1874|cv|1874|cy|1874|da|1874|de|1874|diq|1874|el|1874|eml|1874|eo|1874|es|1874|et|1874|eu|1874|fa|۱۸۷۴|fi|1874|fiu_vro|1874|fo|1874|fr|1874|frp|1874|frr|1874|fur|1874|fy|1874|ga|1874|gan|1874年|gcr|1874|gd|1874|gl|1874|gn|1874|gv|1874|hak|1874-ngièn|he|1874|hi|१८७४|hif|1874|hr|1874.|hsb|1874|ht|1874 (almanak gregoryen)|hu|1874|hy|1874|hyw|1874 թուական|ia|1874|id|1874|ilo|1874|io|1874|is|1874|it|1874|ja|1874年|jv|1874|ka|1874|kaa|1874|kk|1874 жыл|kn|೧೮೭೪|ko|1874년|krc|1874 джыл|ksh|Joohr 1874|ku|1874|kv|1874-ӧд во|la|1874|lb|1874|lez|1874 йис|li|1874|lij|1874|lmo|1874|lt|1874 m.|lv|1874. gads|mai|१८७४|map_bms|1874|mdf|1874|mg|1874|mhr|1874|mi|1874|min|1874|mk|1874|mr|इ.स. १८७४|mrj|1874 и|ms|1874|my|၁၈၇၄|myv|1874 ие|mzn|۱۸۷۴|nah|1874|nap|1874|nds|1874|nds_nl|1874|new|ई सं १८७४|nl|1874|nn|1874|no|1874|nrm|1874|nso|1874|oc|1874|olo|1874|or|୧୮୭୪|os|1874-æм аз|pa|1874|pl|1874|pms|1874|pnb|1874|pt|1874|qu|1874|ro|1874|ru|1874 год|rue|1874|sa|१८७४|sah|1874|scn|1874|sd|1874ع|se|1874|sh|1874.|shn|1874|simple|1874|sk|1874|sl|1874|smn|1874|sq|1874|sr|1874|stq|1874|su|1874|sv|1874|sw|1874|szl|1874|ta|1874|tay|kawas na 1874|te|1874|tet|1874|tg|Соли 1874|th|พ.ศ. 2417|tk|1874|tl|1874|tly|1874|tr|1874|tt|1874 ел|udm|1874 ар|uk|1874|ur|1874ء|uz|1874|vec|1874|vi|1874|vls|1874|vo|1874|wa|1874|war|1874|wuu|1874年|xmf|1874|yi|1874|za|1874 nienz|zea|1874|zh|1874年|zh_classical|一八七四年|zh_min_nan|1874 nî|zh_yue|1874年|qid=Q7761}} another {{ill|Dajōkan Edict|ja|太政官布告・太政官達|ko|태정관포고와 태정관달|qid=Q11444008}} reconfirmed the Yamakawa identification, controversy continued. In {{ill|1881|ab|1881|af|1881|als|1881|am|1881 እ.ኤ.አ.|an|1881|ar|1881|ary|1881|arz|1881|ast|1881|avk|1881|az|1881|azb|۱۸۸۱ (میلادی)|ba|1881 йыл|ban|1881|bar|1881|bat_smg|1881|bcl|1881|be|1881|be_x_old|1881|bg|1881|bn|১৮৮১|bpy|মারি ১৮৮১|br|1881|bs|1881.|ca|1881|cdo|1881 nièng|ce|1881 шо|ceb|1881|ckb|١٨٨١|crh|1881|cs|1881|csb|1881|cv|1881|cy|1881|da|1881|de|1881|diq|1881|el|1881|eml|1881|eo|1881|es|1881|et|1881|eu|1881|fa|۱۸۸۱|fi|1881|fiu_vro|1881|fo|1881|fr|1881|frp|1881|frr|1881|fur|1881|fy|1881|ga|1881|gan|1881年|gcr|1881|gd|1881|gl|1881|gn|1881|gv|1881|hak|1881-ngièn|he|1881|hi|१८८१|hif|1881|hr|1881.|hsb|1881|ht|1881 (almanak gregoryen)|hu|1881|hy|1881|hyw|1881 թուական|ia|1881|id|1881|ilo|1881|io|1881|is|1881|it|1881|ja|1881年|jv|1881|ka|1881|kaa|1881|kk|1881 жыл|kn|೧೮೮೧|ko|1881년|krc|1881 джыл|ksh|Joohr 1881|ku|1881|kv|1881-ӧд во|la|1881|lb|1881|lez|1881 йис|li|1881|lij|1881|lld|1881|lmo|1881|lt|1881 m.|lv|1881. gads|mai|१८८१|map_bms|1881|mdf|1881|mg|1881|mhr|1881|mi|1881|min|1881|mk|1881|ml|1881|mr|इ.स. १८८१|mrj|1881 и|ms|1881|my|၁၈၈၁|myv|1881 ие|mzn|۱۸۸۱|nah|1881|nap|1881|nds|1881|nds_nl|1881|new|ई सं १८८१|nl|1881|nn|1881|no|1881|nrm|1881|nso|1881|oc|1881|olo|1881|or|୧୮୮୧|os|1881-æм аз|pa|1881|pap|1881|pl|1881|pnb|1881|pt|1881|qu|1881|ro|1881|ru|1881 год|rue|1881|sa|१८८१|sah|1881|sc|1881|scn|1881|sd|1881ع|se|1881|sh|1881.|shn|1881|si|1881|simple|1881|sk|1881|sl|1881|smn|1881|sq|1881|sr|1881|stq|1881|su|1881|sv|1881|sw|1881|szl|1881|ta|1881|te|1881|tet|1881|tg|Соли 1881|th|พ.ศ. 2424|tk|1881|tl|1881|tly|1881|tr|1881|tt|1881 ел|udm|1881 ар|uk|1881|ur|1881ء|uz|1881|vec|1881|vi|1881|vls|1881|vo|1881|wa|1881|war|1881|wuu|1881年|xmf|1881|yi|1881|za|1881 nienz|zea|1881|zh|1881年|zh_classical|一八八一年|zh_min_nan|1881 nî|zh_yue|1881年|qid=Q7808}} (Meiji 14), it was changed to Goshō Shrine, but then Yamazaki side strongly objected. As a compromise, the {{ill|Dajōkan|fr|Grand Conseil d'État (époque Meiji)|ja|太政官 (明治時代)|qid=Q125768223|lt=Daijōkan}} ordered establishment of a new shrine site at Tomiura-chō, {{ill|Myōdō District, Tokushima|ceb|Myōdō Gun|es|Distrito de Myōdō|fr|District de Myōdō|id|Distrik Myōdō, Tokushima|it|Distretto di Myōdō|ja|名東郡|ko|묘도군|pl|Powiat Myōdō|uk|Повіт Мьодо|zh|名東郡|qid=Q1156486}} (now Tokushima City). In {{ill|1885|Q7821|qid=Q7821}} (Meiji 18), the current location on the mid-slope of {{ill|Mount Bizan|arz|جبل مونت بيزان|fr|Mont Bizan|ja|眉山 (徳島市)|lld|Mont Bizan|my|ဘိဇန်တောင်|uk|Бідзан (Токусіма)|qid=Q8189109|lt=Mt. Bizan}} was selected; it was temporarily relocated into {{ill|Konpira Shrine (Tokushima)|ja|金刀比羅神社 (徳島市)|qid=Q11646489|lt=Kotohira Shrine}} and Goshō Shrine was made an external sessha. With completion of the shrine buildings, it was moved to the present site on May 15, {{ill|1892|Q7839|qid=Q7839}} (Meiji 25).

For the history of the shikinaisha Inbe Shrine, see {{ill|Inbe Shrine (Yoshinogawa)|Q11490723|qid=Q11490723}}.

=== Rituals ===
* Spring grand festival “Washi-gae” ritual (May 15) - held to commemorate the relocation (founding at the current site) in Meiji 25.

=== Shrine buildings ===
As noted above, the buildings were established in Meiji 25. In {{ill|1945|Q5240|qid=Q5240}} ({{ill|Shōwa era|Q327567|qid=Q327567}} 20), most major buildings were lost in war damage. يىلى|uk|1953|ur|1953ء|uz|1953|vec|1953|vi|1953|vls|1953|vo|1953|wa|1953|war|1953|wuu|1953年|xmf|1953|yi|1953|za|1953 nienz|zea|1953|zh|1953年|zh_classical|一九五三年|zh_min_nan|1953 nî|zh_yue|1953年|qid=Q18585}} (Shōwa 28): front three bays, two bays on each of the other three sides, {{ill|Nagare-zukuri|Q210684|qid=Q210684}} with copper-sheet roof and ridge ornaments (chigi and katsuogi).

=== Sessha: Goshō Shrine ===

=== Aratae cloth ===
According to the {{ill|Engishiki|ar|إنجيشيكي (كتاب ياباني)|de|Engishiki|es|Engishiki|fr|Engishiki|he|אנגישיקי|id|Engishiki|it|Engishiki|ja|延喜式|ko|엔기시키|min|Engishiki|mr|इंगिशिकी|nl|Engishiki|pt|Engishiki|ru|Энгисики|simple|Engishiki|tr|Engishiki|uk|Енґісікі|zh|延喜式|qid=Q1342448}}, Awa {{ill|Inbe clan|fa|خاندان اینبه|ja|忌部氏|pl|Inbe (ród)|simple|Inbe clan|th|ตระกูลอิมเบะ|zh|忌部氏|qid=Q8189229|lt=Inbe}} were to present ''aratae'' (rough hemp cloth woven as divine garments) for the imperial {{ill|Daijosai|Q11433653|qid=Q11433653}} enthronement rite<ref name="週刊神社"/>. Their descendants are said to be the Miki family. At the 1990 Daijōsai, hemp grown in Tokushima was woven at {{ill|Inbe Shrine (Yoshinogawa)|Q11490723|qid=Q11490723|lt=Inbe Shrine}} in Yoshinogawa, and rituals were conducted with the Tokushima-city Inbe Shrine chief priest as celebrant<ref name="週刊神社">{{Cite book|和書|author=|title=Weekly Nihon no Jinja No.67 Inbe Shrine / Ōasahiko Shrine|publisher=DeAgostini Japan|date=2015-5-28|page=}}</ref>.

Torii and bamboo fences were set up in hemp fields; ceremonies included seeding, harvest, first spinning, and first weaving. The selected unmarried weavers wove the cloth, and the finished aratae was placed in a kara-hitsu chest and sent to the Imperial Palace<ref name="週刊神社"/>.
